command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).

VGNODES=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="nodes"{print $2}' vg_structure.tsv)
VGLEN=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="graph_total_length"{print $2}' vg_structure.tsv)
printf 'vg_nodes\t%s\n' "$VGNODES"
printf 'vg_total_length\t%s\n' "$VGLEN"
test -n "$VGNODES" -a -n "$VGLEN" || { echo "FAIL: no structure carried from the vg task"; exit 1; }

odgi version 2>&1 | head -2

echo "== convert the same graph with an unrelated implementation =="
# odgi is a separate codebase with its own graph representation. Converting vg's output and
# recovering the SAME node count and total sequence length is a cross-code structural check:
# two independent implementations agreeing on what the graph contains.
odgi build -g chr20.gfa -o chr20.og -P > build.log 2>&1
RC=$?
printf 'odgi_build_rc\t%s\n' "$RC"
test "$RC" = "0" || { tail -25 build.log; echo "FAIL: odgi build exited $RC"; exit 1; }

odgi stats -i chr20.og -S > odgi_stats.txt 2>&1
cat odgi_stats.txt | sed 's/^/  /'

# odgi stats -S prints a header line then values; pull by column NAME, and strip the leading
# '#' the first column carries -- odgi writes "#length  nodes  edges  paths  steps", so a
# lookup for "length" misses, awk returns field 0, and $0 is the WHOLE LINE. That is the same
# leading-'#' convention cfgrib and PLINK 2's #CHROM use; it is worth handling by reflex.
ONODES=$(awk 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){k=$i; sub(/^#/,"",k); h[k]=i} next} {print $(h["nodes"])}' odgi_stats.txt)
OLEN=$(awk 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){k=$i; sub(/^#/,"",k); h[k]=i} next} {print $(h["length"])}' odgi_stats.txt)
OEDGES=$(awk 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){k=$i; sub(/^#/,"",k); h[k]=i} next} {print $(h["edges"])}' odgi_stats.txt)
# A field that came back as the whole line means the lookup missed; fail loudly rather than
# comparing a line against a number.
case "$OLEN" in *[!0-9]*) echo "FAIL: parsed total length as '$OLEN' -- the header lookup missed"; exit 1;; esac
case "$ONODES" in *[!0-9]*) echo "FAIL: parsed node count as '$ONODES'"; exit 1;; esac
printf 'odgi_edges\t%s\n' "$OEDGES"
printf 'odgi_nodes\t%s\n' "$ONODES"
printf 'odgi_total_length\t%s\n' "$OLEN"
test -n "$ONODES" -a -n "$OLEN" || { echo "FAIL: could not read odgi stats columns"; exit 1; }

test "$OLEN" = "$VGLEN" || {
  echo "FAIL: odgi reports $OLEN total bases, vg reported $VGLEN -- the two implementations"
  echo "      disagree about what the graph contains"; exit 1; }
printf 'identity_length\tvg and odgi agree on total graph sequence (%s bases)\n' "$OLEN"

# Node and edge counts are preserved too. Worth stating precisely what that proves: odgi
# honours the segmentation declared in the GFA rather than re-deriving its own, so this is two
# implementations agreeing on how to READ a graph, not independently choosing the same node
# boundaries. The total-length agreement above is the stronger of the two claims.
test "$ONODES" = "$VGNODES" || { echo "FAIL: odgi read $ONODES nodes from a GFA vg wrote with $VGNODES"; exit 1; }
printf 'identity_nodes\tvg and odgi agree on node count (%s)\n' "$ONODES"

{ printf 'observable\tvalue\n'
  printf 'vg_nodes\t%s\nvg_total_length\t%s\n' "$VGNODES" "$VGLEN"
  printf 'odgi_nodes\t%s\nodgi_edges\t%s\nodgi_total_length\t%s\n' "$ONODES" "$OEDGES" "$OLEN"; } > score.tsv
cp score.tsv pangenome-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "ODGI OK"
